html:
The Palaiologos family was the last dynasty of the Byzantine Empire, ruling from 1259 until the fall of Constantinople in 1453, the longest of any Byzantine dynasty.

Its founder, Michael VIII, retook Constantinople from the Latins in 1261. His heirs ruled a shrinking state, weakened by civil wars such as the war of 1341 to 1347. Land grants to soldiers, the pronoia, became hereditary. After the Ottomans took Gallipoli in 1354, the emperors became their vassals.

  • Manuel II toured the West seeking help.
  • John VIII accepted union with Rome at Florence in 1439.
  • Constantine XI died on the walls in 1453.

The age still saw a late flowering of art, seen in the Chora Church mosaics.
